messages:
elaine: Kicking off the multi-PR docs refactor now. I split changes into targeted PRs to keep previews quick and reviews focused. Will open in waves and do a small canary first.

sam: drop PR links when ready. I can take the file-move reviews and watch for anchor churn.

elaine: PRs opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1901 (file moves), /1902 (redirects), /1903 (sdk-snippets), /1904 (examples), /1905 (anchor fixes + TOC). Preview hub: https://docs-preview.redwood.ai/ (use the PR selector).

maria: I’m owning redirects (/1902) and the reindex checklist. I’ll produce a mapping CSV and a validator script. Ping me when /1901 preview is green.

docsbot: preview built for /1901 - https://docs-preview.redwood.ai/pr-1901 - status: green, lint: 2 warnings (mdx link style)

sam: noted the MDX warnings. Reminder: file moves will change anchors and slugs; strict redirect coverage and an anchor-validator run are required before merge.

elaine: Proposed ordered merge sequence (must be followed):
1) /1901 (file moves) - canary subset first
2) /1902 (redirects) - full mapping must exist for all moved paths
3) /1903 (sdk-snippets) - update snippet outputs and CI runner
4) /1904 (examples) - content tweaks and walkthrough updates
5) /1905 (anchor + TOC fixes) - final pass, then trigger search reindex

jordan: Which merge window are we aiming for? mid-week daytime preferable.

tim: Scheduled window: Wed 09:30 PT. I’ll enforce branch protection requiring "docs-preview:green" and prevent merges outside the window.

oliver: For the canary, recommend moving ~8-12 pages across SDK, API, and Quickstart so we cover varied slugs and TOCs. I can watch search behavior.

sam: Canary plan works. If any redirect or anchor fails we add label "hold/merge-block" and halt. Also leaving inline PR comments for TOC link updates.

ci-bot: CI statuses: /1901: success, /1902: building preview, /1903: lint failed (snippet mismatch), /1904: success, /1905: pending

elaine: I’ll address the snippet mismatch in /1903 this afternoon and re-run. Tagging @sam @maria for review after fixes. :eyes:

sam: Pre-merge checks I run locally:
python tools/linkcheck.py docs/ --anchors --report=anchors.csv
scripts/simulate_search_index.sh > search-sim.out

maria: Redirect mapping format for the validator: one JSON object per line:
{"from":"/old/path","to":"/new/path","status":"301"}
I’ll add scripts/redirect_coverage.py to assert every moved path has a mapping.

docsbot: preview notice: search results in PR preview currently show old titles for moved pages. Post-merge reindex will update results on the live site.

elaine: Important: do NOT trigger a full search reindex during the merge window. Platform will run the reindex as a controlled post-merge job and warm the CDN.

sam: small nit: some TOC entries in /1901 still reference old anchors. I’ll leave inline comments on the PR.

oliver: Ops question: how quickly do redirect mappings propagate to the edge? CDN TTL and warm steps?

maria: CDN redirect config TTL is ~60s. Platform will push and warm configs as part of the post-merge hook.

ci-bot: builds updated: /1901: success, /1902: success, /1903: success, /1904: success, /1905: success (previews ready)

elaine: Canary timeline: Wed 09:30 PT merge 10 pages from /1901 plus partial redirects in /1902 for those paths. Monitor 30 minutes, then proceed if no issues.

jordan: I’ll join the post-merge watch rotation. If anything looks off I’ll apply "hold/merge-block" and ping #release-war-room.

sam: starting reviews now, posting inline comments. Keep replies concise so authors can iterate quickly.

elaine: Thanks team. Reconvene here after canary. Please avoid unrelated merges to main during the window. :rocket:
